Claim:
On-screen caption "FIERY BUT MOSTLY PEACEFUL PROTESTS AFTER POLICE SHOOTING" shown over burning vehicles and buildings in Kenosha, WI.
Began: Aug 25, 2020 (CNN Early Start, ~5:05 AM ET / 3:05 AM MDT) | Ended: single broadcast segment
Who_Pushed_It: CNN (Early Start with Christine Romans and Laura Jarrett)
Notes: The caption ran over live footage of structures on fire. In the same segment, correspondent Omar Jimenez said 'what you're seeing is one of multiple locations that have been burning in Kenosha' and contrasted the night with daytime demonstrations he called 'largely peaceful.' Anchor Christine Romans said 'At least three buildings were on fire in Kenosha overnight.' The caption described the scene on screen as mostly peaceful while it showed arson. The reporter's spoken words did separate day from night. It aired Aug 25, not Aug 24. ACLED's nationwide 'mostly peaceful' aggregate ends Aug 22 and does not cover Kenosha.

Claim:
Seattle's Capitol Hill protest zone was "more like a block party atmosphere. It's not an armed takeover"; "there is no threat right now to the public"; "We could have the Summer of Love."
Began: Jun 11, 2020 (CNN Cuomo Prime Time) | Ended: Jul 1, 2020 (zone cleared under Mayor's emergency order)
Notes: The quotes are exact from CNN's transcript. Durkan's own Executive Order 2020-08 (June 30) later recorded several things: 'A pervasive presence of firearms and other weapons has been well-documented'; a 525% increase in person-related crime in the area June 2-30 vs. 2019; homicides on June 20 and June 29; and first responders 'denied safe access ... by hostile crowds, including armed individuals.' CAVEAT: the remarks were made June 11, before both homicides. 'Summer of Love' answered a question about how long the zone would last and was partly speculative. The EO's crime window (June 2-30) overlaps the interview date. The EO itself also says 'much of the expression has been peaceful.' Rate as misleading only on the 'no threat ... to the public' / 'not an armed takeover' portion. Do not rate the 'Summer of Love' phrase alone.

Claim:
SPD radio traffic reported that a group of Proud Boys was marching downtown and moving toward the CHOP.
Began: Jun 8, 2020 (~9:24 PM PT) | Ended: disclosed by OPA investigation (2020OPA-0479), published in Seattle OIG Sentinel Event Review Oct 2022
Who_Pushed_It: Seattle Police Department (an SPD Captain, per OPA)
Approximate_Duration: ~2 years until the public review (OPA finding earlier)
Notes: The Seattle OIG Sentinel Event Review Wave 3 reports that 'an SPD Captain appointed an officer to make false radio broadcasts to draw protestors away from the CHOP.' OPA found that the broadcasts violated SPD policy. The review says some protesters armed themselves in response.

Claim:
SPD said at a June 10, 2020 press conference that it had 'heard anecdotally reports' of businesses in the CHOP being extorted.
Began: Jun 10, 2020 | Ended: No ending date
Notes: The Sentinel Event Review found: 'No police reports were filed related to extortion of businesses within or around the CHOP.' This shows the claim was never substantiated by reports. It does not prove that no extortion occurred.

Claim:
Those arrested in the Minneapolis-St. Paul rioting were from out of state. St. Paul Mayor Carter said essentially everyone arrested the prior night was from out of state; Gov. Walz estimated about 80% of those causing damage were from outside Minnesota.
Began: May 30, 2020 (state press conference) | Ended: May 30-31, 2020 (Carter walked it back)
Who_Pushed_It: St. Paul Mayor Melvin Carter; Gov. Tim Walz (May 30, 2020 news conference)
Notes: HOLD. The Minnesota Senate report states 'It was primarily Minnesotans from the metropolitan area who were arrested for inciting the violence.' The officials' exact words have NOT yet been verified from the original video: C-SPAN program 547309 returned 403 to automated fetch, and the quotes come from Poynter/CBS/KARE leads. Confirm the exact wording from the C-SPAN or KARE 11 video before publishing. If confirmed, Carter's statement is 'Proven false' (he retracted it). Walz's '80%' is an estimate that jail records did not support.

Claim:
George Floyd died of a drug (fentanyl) overdose, not from police restraint.
Began: 2020 | Ended: No ending date (still repeated)
Who_Pushed_It: ATTRIBUTION NEEDED - no primary-source instance by a named official or outlet was collected. (Chauvin's appellate brief argued the fentanyl level was 'three times the amount considered fatal', but that is litigation advocacy, not a public claim.)
Notes: HOLD. The record contradicts the claim as stated. The HCME certified homicide, with fentanyl as an 'other significant condition.' The AFME concurred. The jury, the MN Court of Appeals, and Judge Cahill (who found Dr. Fowler's conclusions 'unpersuasive') all ruled against it, and Chauvin admitted in his federal plea that his force 'impaired Mr. Floyd's ability to obtain and maintain sufficient oxygen.' The record ALSO contains true facts that must be shown: Baker called fentanyl 11 'pretty high'; a prosecutor memo summarized it as 'a fatal level of fentanyl under normal circumstances'; and Baker testified he would certify fentanyl toxicity if Floyd had been found home alone with no other findings. Do not publish without a named, primary-sourced pusher.
